name: open-research-index
description: Search papers, preprints and formal proofs, and read what experts said about each, with sources.

interface.shortDescription: Papers beside what experts said about them
interface.longDescription: Open Research Index lists papers, preprints and formal proofs: AI-generated research such as OpenAI's mathematics release and agenticpapers.app, Lean formalization registries, and this year's arXiv in math, quant-ph and hep-th. Each record sits beside the expert responses the index has linked to it (arXiv replies, blog posts, talks, MathOverflow answers and X posts), each with its author, its date, a quote read from the source and a link. Ask about a paper and the assistant can find its record and show who responded and what they said. Read-only, no account needed. It covers only what the index holds: a record with no responses means none have been linked, not that none exist.
defaultPrompt: What did mathematicians say about OpenAI's quasi-Riemann hypothesis paper?
Which AI-generated papers got expert responses most recently?
Has anyone checked OpenAI's matrix multiplication exponent paper?
